ISSUE TITLE: The operation "stream" EXCEPT "static" is allowed but does not work as expected
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
DataFrame has several "set" operations e.g. UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT (MINUS) which performs set operations between two DataFrames.

But the allowance of streaming vs batch (static) DataFrame for left and right is different depending on the operator.
 * UNION: batch-batch and stream-stream is allowed, mix of stream and batch isn't allowed.
 * INTERSECT: stream isn't allowed, hence only batch-batch is allowed.
 * EXCEPT: stream on the right side isn't allowed, so batch-batch and stream-batch are allowed.

We just found out the allowed case of EXCEPT, stream-batch, is very poorly defined and it does not work as expected in most cases.

Here is the semantic of EXCEPT DISTINCT vs EXCEPT ALL.

  - EXCEPT DISTINCT returns values present in L but absent from R, with duplicates removed.
  - EXCEPT ALL preserves multiplicity. For each value, it returns max(count(L) - count(R), 0) copies.

  Example:

  L = [A, A, A, B]
  R = [A, A, C]

  Results:

  EXCEPT DISTINCT = [B]
  EXCEPT ALL      = [A, B]

ISSUE TITLE: Spread NULL left anti join keys across shuffle partitions
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
SPARK-56903 added feature-flagged NULL-key spreading for shuffled outer equi-joins. The review discussion explicitly identified ordinary LEFT ANTI joins as a follow-up because the same structural condition applies: left-side rows with NULL keys cannot match under `=`, but they must be emitted by the anti join. Hash partitioning currently sends all of those rows to one reducer, causing avoidable skew on NULL-heavy inputs.

Extend `spark.sql.shuffle.spreadNullJoinKeys.enabled` to ordinary shuffled LEFT ANTI equi-joins when the preserved left-side join keys are nullable. Non-NULL keys should retain normal hash partitioning, while NULL-keyed rows can use the existing null-aware shuffle layout. LEFT SEMI and other existence joins remain out of scope because they do not emit unmatched left rows.

Add correctness and physical-partitioning coverage for sort-merge join and shuffled hash join, plus AQE coverage for coalesced null-aware partitioning.

Related discussion: https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/55927#discussion_r3261128231

ISSUE TITLE: Spread NULL outer join keys across shuffle partitions
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
Spark currently hashes all join keys, including NULL keys, when planning shuffle exchanges for ordinary outer equi-joins. For rows whose join key is NULL, ordinary equality predicates such as left.k = right.k can never match. However, those rows still hash to the same shuffle partition, which can create avoidable reducer skew when an outer-side input contains many NULL keys.

Why this should change:
- Non-NULL keys still need normal hash co-location so matching rows meet in the same reducer.
- NULL-key rows under ordinary equality are semantically unmatched, so they do not need to be co-located with each other.
- Spreading only those NULL-key rows across shuffle partitions preserves query semantics while reducing a common skew pattern for outer joins.

Examples:
1. LEFT OUTER JOIN
   Suppose the left side contains millions of rows where k IS NULL, and the join predicate is left.k = right.k. Those rows can never match the right side, but today they are funneled into the same shuffle partition. They should be spread across partitions instead.

ISSUE TITLE: StreamsGroupHeartbeatRequest.Builder does not clear owned warm-up tasks when it negotiates request version 0
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
`StreamsGroupHeartbeatRequest.Builder.build(short)` clears `TaskOffsets` and `TaskEndOffsets` when the negotiated request version is 0, but does not clear `WarmupTasks`. At the same time, a 4.2 or 4.3 broker rejects a heartbeat that reports a non-empty set of owned warm-up tasks.

So a client that owns a warm-up task and then negotiates RPC version 0 has every heartbeat rejected with `InvalidRequestException`. The client cannot clear the task on its own, because dropping it requires an assignment, and an assignment only arrives in a heartbeat response. Restarting the member recovers, since a re-joining member reports no owned tasks.

This bug does not affect 4.4 directly, because we don't assign warmup tasks yet, however, the bug will surface with 4.5 release: KS 4.4 is "warmup task ready" and thus a 4.5 broker might assign warmup tasks to a 4.4 client. If the broker get downgraded afterward to 4.3/4.2, the 4.4 client would report its warmups to the broker, and the broker reject the heartbeat.

ISSUE TITLE: Make PandasMode collation-aware
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
pandas_mode(the internal expression behind the Pandas API on Spark Series.mode() / DataFrame.mode()) silently returns wrong results on non-binary collated strings.

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

ISSUE TITLE: Time Based Priority for BucketCache
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
This Jira introduces the feature of time-based priority in BucketCache, where a configurable "age" is used as a threshold limit for data caching. Data blocks with a more recent age then this limit should be kept in the cache, while older data would be picked for eviction (or not considered for caching). The data age based priority would be applied when deciding if a block should be added to BucketCache (i.e. during reads, writes, compaction and prefetch), as well as during the cache freeSpace run (mass eviction), before applying the LRU logic. 

Because blocks don't hold any specific meta information other than type, it's necessary to group blocks of same "age group" on separate files. DateTieredCompaction can be configured to provide two windows (one older and one younger than the threshold limit), so that a cell timestamp based age priority can be implemented. ISSUE TITLE: ConsumerGroup static member rejoin can fail with GroupMaxSizeReachedException at max size
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
GroupMetadataManager#throwIfConsumerGroupIsFull() only checks whether the provided memberId already exists in the group:

{code:java}
  group.numMembers() >= config.consumerGroupMaxSize()
      && (memberId.isEmpty() || !group.hasMember(memberId))
{code}

However, when a static member rejoins after leaving with the static leave epoch (-2), the rejoining member may use a new member ID. In that case, the existing static member is identified by instanceId, not by the new memberId.

Because the max-size check runs before resolving/replacing the static member, a valid static member rejoin can be rejected with GroupMaxSizeReachedException when the group is already at max size, even though the operation would replace an existing static member and would not increase the group size.

*Expected behavior*

A static member rejoin for an existing instanceId should not fail the max-size check solely because the rejoining memberId is new or empty. The check should account for existing static members, similar to checking group.hasStaticMember(instanceId).

ISSUE TITLE: A delayed EndTxn message can cause aborted read, lost writes, atomicity violation
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
In short: I believe that both an internal retry mechanism and guidance from the example code and client API docs are independently capable of causing committed transactions to actually abort, aborted transactions to actually commit, and transactions to be split into multiple parts with different fates. A delayed EndTxn message could arrive seconds later and decide the fate of an unrelated transaction.

Consider the attached Lamport diagram, reconstructed from node logs and packet captures in a recent Jepsen test. In it, a single process, using a single producer and consumer, executes a series of transactions which all commit or abort cleanly. Process 76 selected the unique transactional ID `jt1234` on initialization.

From packet captures and debug logs, we see `jt1234` used producer ID `233`, submitted all four operations, then sent an EndTxn message with `committed = false`, which denotes a transaction abort. However, fifteen separate calls to `poll` observed this transaction's write of `424` to key `5`---an obvious case of aborted read (G1a). Even stranger, *no* poller observed the other writes from this transaction: key `17` apparently never
received values `926` or `927`.

You are planning release '6.0-alpha3' for project CASSANDRA.

BACKLOG CANDIDATES:
- Non printable characters in the log for Gossiper
- Compression dictionary training fails with "insufficient samples" on large-chunk tables (SSTableChunkSampler per-SSTable allocation rounds to zero)

- Fixes for fully-expired SSTable index notification in compaction
- Concurrent SAI vector inserts fail with "Number of outstanding pooled objects has gone beyond the limit" since CASSANDRA-21160
- Upgrade async-profiler to 4.5
- The commit log allocator never observes the shutdown state, so a prepared segment can leak
- CI: generateTestReports queues behind the test fan-out, agent pods churn instead of queueing, and reports on split balance
- Reduce CI console output volume
- Guardrail values of zero to mean literally zero
- support multi-cell columns
- Optimize BatchStatement.authorize for the case when a single table is updated
- IndexTermType#comparator() Handles Reversed Types Incorrectly
- Upgrade lz4-java to v1.11.2 
- Remove superfluous build scripts CASSANDRA-21301 introduced
- Improve Incremental Repair documentation clarity
- Update Cassandra Installation Docs to reflect Python 3.13 support for cqlsh
- Allow schema transformation CQL larger than 32kb
- Add guardrails or hard limits for CMS size
- Node can report DECOMMISSION_FAILED while actively leaving after a rejected decommission attempt
- NoSpamLogger uses unbounded cache that could lead to memory exhaustion
- Force repair should ignore min_repair_interval
- isOrdinaryUser check performed by Guardrail.enabled is expensive
- MultiStepOperations should not encode range movements using endpoints
- Make sure counter writes are not unnecessarily failed during epoch bumps
- /etc/cassandra/cassandra-jaas.config does not exist in Packages install
- .build/docker scripts refuse to run without timeout, which they never invoke
- AST fuzz testing support for LIKE/prefix queries
- Add byte for byte test harness to detect and resolve cursor deviations from iterator path
- Stop using Java streams in CIDRPermissions.SubsetPermissions#canAccessFrom hot method
- Update testing and CI documentation
- CI: Prevent/kill Jenkins k8s agent orphans and unschedulable agent pods
- truncateBlocking silently succeeds when runWithCompactionsDisabled returns null
- Enable trickle_fsync by default
- Protect uncaught_exceptions virtual table against the crash path
- Validate authz before performing role check in LIST ROLES/PERMISSIONS
- Consistency can be violated when bootstrap or decommission is resumed after node restart
- SAI support for blob CQL type
- Masked columns cannot be deserialized from cluster metadata, preventing node startup
- Regression in PasswordObfuscator for dollar-quoted passwords
- Avoid Rebuilding Per-SSTable SAI Components Unless Missing or Corrupted
- Caffeine caches in CompressionDictionaryCache and ZstdDictionaryCompressor should specify an executor explicitly 
- trickle_fsync is silently ignored for compressed SSTables
- Allow setCompressedReadAheadBufferSizeInKb(0) to disable RAB
- cqlsh prompt does not reset to default after dropping the current keyspace
- Implement CMS rediscovery and recovery protocol
- MemtableReclaimMemory AssertionError: Negative released is possible in case of non-leaf-only B-tree update
- Throw CorruptSSTableException in fill()
- Read repairs can break row isolation
- nodetool verify is broken
- InvalidRequestException: Key may not be empty
- dead Small OutboundTcpConnection to restarted nodes blocking hint delivery
- Performance improvement of Cassandra UDF/UDA
- OOM when using SASI index
- Bulk Reading from Cassandra
- Overload because of hint pressure + MVs
- Instances from a 2nd ring join another ring when running on the same nodes 
- Schema version mismatch may leads to Casandra OOM at bootstrap during a rolling upgrade process

You are planning release 'kubernetes-operator-1.16.0' for project FLINK.

BACKLOG CANDIDATES:
- Autoscaler parallelism overrides serialized in the operator's YAML dialect break job submission for Flink 1.x jobs
- Flink 2.0 job configuration response cannot be parsed by the operator
- Application cluster: FINISHED FlinkDeployment falls back to RECONCILING if JM pod is lost/recreated
- Add connect / read timeout to K8s operator artifact fetcher
- Harden autoscaler metrics name parsing against complex regex
- Autoscaler state ConfigMap is treated as trusted input
- Harden job artifact fetching in kubernetes operator
- Fix NOTICE files to match dependencies for Flink Kubernetes Operator
- Autoscaling example classes leak into the operator javadoc site
- Protect against large autoscaler config maps
- Source parallelism is not capped at the partition count
- flink-kubernetes-operator bundles vulnerable logback-core 1.2.13 (CVE-2024-12798, CVE-2025-11226, CVE-2026-1225)
- Document the runtime configuration and stop jobs from overriding operator config through it
- Redeploying a FlinkSessionJob from an explicit savepoint fails if the job was previously suspended
- Operator API tests: kube-API-server tests silently skipped in CI (Tests run: 0)
- Add logic to override observed config based on settings observed through REST API
- Helm chart silently ignores defaultConfiguration.config.yaml; always mounts flink-conf.yaml from chart defaults
- flink-kubernetes-operator: Bump jackson-bom to 2.21.5 to retire 11 advisories
- FlinkStateSnapshot cleanup fails with NPE when status is null, permanently blocking CR and namespace deletion
- Operator serializes managed-deployment config in its own YAML dialect, breaking Flink 1.x deployments when the operator itself runs on standard config.yaml
- [FKO] Adopt AI-assisted contribution guidelines for the Kubernetes Operator
- FlinkSessionJob's lifecycleState stays "UPGRADING" even after it's suspended successfully
- AbstractFlinkService.deleteBlocking() swallows KubernetesClientTimeoutException allowing cluster upgrade to proceed on top of still-running cluster
- Fast-running FlinkSessionJob does not reflect actual state of the job
- Improve Flink Kubernetes Operator documentation coverage
- Upgrade operator to Java Operator SDK version 5.5
- Kubernetes Operator: run Helm chart CI and e2e tests on Helm 4 
- Blue/Green: after an aborted transition, the next deploy deletes Blue immediately instead of waiting the deletion delay
- BlueGreen transition should finalize immediately after deleting previous deployment
- Do not use "--host" CLI param for standalone job
- Logging framework JARs are placed under $FLINK_HOME/log instead of the operator lib directory
- Move FlinkResourceValidator and FlinkResourceMutator to the api module
- Group example modules under an examples aggregator pom
- Improve the autoscaler context structure and propagation
- FLIP-586: Composable Parallelism Alignment Modes for Flink Autoscaler
- FlinkStateSnapshot with default backoffLimit=-1 (documented as "unlimited retries") never retries and fails immediately on first error
- Replace taskManager/jobmanager.resource with resources conforming to ResourceRequirements
- Autoscaler Flink REST client timeout is silently overridden by the operator client timeout
- [JUnit5 Migration] Upgrade Testcontainers to 2.0.5 - flink-autoscaler-plugin-jdbc
- FLIP-575: Scaling Executor Plugin SPI for Flink Autoscaler
- Delegation Token expire after enable delegation token framework
- Invalid ConfigOption for "aws.credentials.provider.role.provider" in AWSConfigOptions
- Breaking changes for Flink 3.0
- Define ConfigOption for aws, scan and sink map in Kinesis
- The new CSV source (file system source + CSV format) does not support reading files whose file encoding is not UTF-8
- CommittableMessageTypeInfo#toString may force client to have S3 credentials
- JobMasterPartitionTrackerImpl#requestShuffleDescriptorsFromResourceManager blocks main thread
- The asyncOperationsThreadPool in SubtaskCheckpointCoordinatorImpl can only create one worker thread
- python_job.py should write to TEST_DATA_DIR
- TwoInputStreamTaskTest.testWatermarkAndWatermarkStatusForwarding failed
